subject: Queued-burst reconciliation: backoff, routing, and customer readout
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, ops@flowmart.com
Cc: product@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Queued-burst reconciliation: observed p95 spike for FlowMart + ask

Morning all —

We saw a brief but sharp p95 increase for FlowMart starting ~08:57 PST (see attached snapshot). Impact window was ~08:57–09:05: user-facing latency for their GenAPI route jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s, and we observed a concurrent token-queue depth spike on the checkout path. No error-rate increase, just elevated tail latency and queued tokens.

FlowMart is on dedicated capacity but uses opportunistic warm instances for peak bursts; their client-side retries/backoff behavior is fairly aggressive (short initial backoff + linear increments). Initial correlation suggests a queued-burst — many simultaneous short requests that hold KV caches and briefly starve downstream execution.

Immediate asks:
- Ben/Karthik: can SRE confirm whether this is queue buildup (fanout) vs. kernel scheduling? Attachments: snapshot-queued-burst-20270630.json (token histograms + instance queue depths).
- Product (Kimberly/Marissa): recommend whether we want to enable a temporary gateway-level throttle for FlowMart while we triage, or prefer to surface a customer note first.
- Ops (FlowMart): can you confirm if any recent client rollout changed retries/backoff? Samir — tagging you here.

I’m drafting a short customer-facing note but want alignment before we send.

Thanks,
Jordan
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, ops@flowmart.com
Cc: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Queued-burst reconciliation: observed p95 spike for FlowMart + ask

Jordan — thanks for the flag and the snapshot. Quick notes from the triage so far: 

1) Evidence: instance-level queue depth (per-GPU token queue) shows a 6x spike across 3 of the 5 warm instances serving FlowMart at 08:56–08:59. Kernel scheduling latency stayed within expected bounds once dequeued. That points to queueing/fanout, not kernel regressions.

2) Root cause hypothesis: an upstream client rollout reduced initial retry/backoff from 50ms -> 20ms and switched to a linear retry pattern. Under high concurrency this creates many overlapping short-lived requests that occupy prefix/KV resources and cause token-queue head-of-line blocking.

3) Mitigations we can act on immediately (order based on speed/risk):
   - Gateway-level short backpressure for FlowMart (throttle to preserve p50/p90; keeps requests under the warm-instance capacity).
   - Adjust per-instance queue depth threshold to temporarily allow a slightly higher in-flight concurrency on dedicated instances (risk: slightly higher p50 under extreme load).
   - Routing tweak: prefer warm instances with populated KV caches and reject to cold nodes (fast, low-risk).
   - Client ask: recommend FlowMart increase initial backoff to 60ms and exponential backoff jitter.

I can push the routing tweak and the gateway throttle asap (need prod-ops approval). Will follow up with a short runbook entry and the expected SLO delta for each mitigation.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Queued-burst reconciliation: observed p95 spike for FlowMart + ask

Thanks, Ben — that diagnosis makes sense. A couple product considerations before we push any customer-facing changes: 

- Gateway throttle: acceptable as a short-term protection, but we need clear rollback conditions (e.g., sustained CPU < 60% and instance queue depths back to baseline for 30min). Also, include a per-minute limit so we don't overly penalize legitimate traffic bursts.

- Routing tweak: can we make this opt-in per-customer for dedicated customers? FlowMart paid for predictable capacity, and a routing change that favors cached warm nodes is consistent with that expectation. If we do opt-in, product will update the Dedicated docs and create a configuration flag.

- Prefix caching: enabling more aggressive prefix+KV caching for FlowMart could reduce repeated cold starts. What's the memory impact? (Ben/Karthik please advise).

I attached a draft of a short customer note (draft-customer-note-FlowMart-20270630.md) that calls out: what happened, immediate steps we took, expected customer impact, and recommended client-side changes. Please review — I want to send within the hour if SRE confirms no further risk.

Kimberly Park
PM, Serving & Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@flowmart.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Queued-burst reconciliation: observed p95 spike for FlowMart + ask

Thanks for the quick triage and the draft note — appreciate the transparency. A few datapoints from our side: we did push a client adjustment to the SDK this morning that reduced the initial backoff (we rolled it to canary users at 07:50 PST). That matches what you observed.

We prefer an opt-in routing change and would like the temporary gateway throttle only if it defaults to a conservative per-minute cap (we'll take a small increase in p50 if it protects p95).

Can you confirm:
- ETA for the routing change and gateway throttle?
- Will any changes affect data retention/audit logs? We need to preserve request traces for 30 days for our internal compliance.

If the routing tweak can be opt-in and non-destructive, we approve trying it. Also open to receiving a formal recommended backoff pattern we can push to the SDK.

—Samir
Ops Lead, FlowMart
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@flowmart.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: product@redwood.ai, sre-oncall@redwood.ai, solutions@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan and readout — FlowMart queued-burst (08:57 window)

Team / Samir — thanks for the fast confirmations. Final consolidated plan and timeline below: 

1) Immediate (T+0–10m) — SRE (Ben) will apply routing preference to favor warm instances for FlowMart and enable a conservative gateway-level throttle (cap: 180 rps sustained, 360 burst) to protect p95. This should be non-disruptive to successful requests and will avoid head-of-line queueing. Expected SLO delta: p95 should fall < 400ms within 5–10 minutes.

2) Short-term (T+1–3h) — Product will enable opt-in routing preference flag for Dedicated tenants; we will enable it for FlowMart today and document the behavior. Also will run a memory estimate for prefix caching; Ben/Karthik, please provide the memory delta within the hour.

3) Customer coordination (T+0.5–1h) — Kimberly to send the customer note (attached) that explains root cause, actions taken, and recommended client-side backoff (we recommend initial backoff 60ms + exponential with jitter). Jordan will coordinate a short post-mortem readout call if FlowMart requests one.

4) Follow-up (T+24–72h) — Monitor queue depths and latency; if we see recurrence we will roll back the throttle and escalate to a deeper kernel scheduling investigation. Rollback conditions (gateway throttle off): 30m stable queues at baseline and CPU < 60% across serving fleet.

Samir — preserving traces for 30 days is fine; changes will not purge logs. Ben will upload a concise runbook entry (DOCS-4872) and the snapshot we used for triage.

Next steps: Ben to announce when routing+throttle are live; Kimberly to send the customer note; Jordan to schedule a 30m sync if FlowMart wants it.

Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
